corrections.source_says: The form rules require this object for every diversity outcome. Record a qualitative visual comparison of clustering in the CLIP embedding plot, computed over first and final images across participants within each tool condition. The figure labels its axes PC1 and PC2; the exact embedding checkpoint and projection procedure are not specified. No numerical between-person diversity metric or uncertainty estimate is reported. Appendix D.7 names OpenCLIP for the first-to-final analysis, but its cosine-similarity definition conflicts with the main text's L2-distance definition; retain that caveat and do not treat the within-session means as a between-person diversity estimate.

confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion, including references and Appendices A-E, and checked the relevant PDF text and Figure 4; the PDF has 18 pages and is stamped arXiv:2604.13956v1, 15 Apr 2026 (PDF p. 1; Appendices A-E, pp. 13-18).
The title and five author names, including their order, match the source metadata and title page (PDF p. 1).

The evaluated study is a remotely moderated within-participant comparison of progressive Creo and a multi-turn prompt-centric ChatGPT image interface; each participant used both tools on different living-room/kitchen prompts (PDF p. 7, Section 4.1; p. 15, Appendix D.2).

Tool and prompt order were counterbalanced with four listed sequences, but neither the main text nor the appendix states random allocation or how participants were allocated to sequences; has_randomized_people_study=false means randomization is not established, rather than proven absent (PDF p. 7, Section 4.1; p. 15, Appendix D.2 and Table 2).

The reported study sample is 15 people, and Figure 4 displays P1-P15 in both conditions; the two arm counts refer to the same people, so the sample is below the 50-person core threshold (PDF p. 7, Section 4.1.1; p. 8, Figure 4).

Appendix D.1 reports 275 screening responses and 19 invited participants; those are screening and invitation counts, not randomized or analyzed counts, and the transition to the reported study sample is unexplained (PDF p. 14, Appendix D.1; p. 7, Section 4.1.1).

Randomized-person counts are not reported and should remain null; the form appropriately retains design_class=other, randomized=not_stated, core=no, and context_class=none rather than inferring randomization or established non-random allocation from counterbalancing (PDF p. 7, Section 4.1; p. 15, Appendix D.2 and Table 2; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 3-4).

The participants had visual-design experience, and Appendix C explicitly describes an architecture student from the user study, supporting the mixed population description (PDF p. 7, Section 4.1.1; p. 13, Appendix C).
The stated task duration is approximately 14 minutes per condition within an approximately 60-minute remote session (PDF p. 7, Sections 4.1.1-4.1.2; p. 15, Appendix D.3).
The anchoring reported string and one-line finding reproduce the main-text statistics exactly: Creo M = 0.75, SD = 0.13; GPT M = 0.46, SD = 0.31 (PDF p. 8, Section 4.3.1).

Those numerical distances compare the first and final images within each participant session and are aggregated across participants; they do not quantify similarity between different people (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2; p. 8, Section 4.3.1 and Figure 4; p. 16, Appendix D.7).

The form correctly flags the source inconsistency: the main text defines L2 distance between unit-norm CLIP embeddings, whereas Appendix D.7 specifies cosine similarity with OpenCLIP and L2-normalized embeddings (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2; p. 16, Appendix D.7).

The diversity reported string accurately describes the qualitative Figure 4 caption; no numerical between-person diversity contrast or inferential test is supplied (PDF p. 8, Figure 4 and Section 4.3.1; p. 16, Appendix D.7).

The source supports Creo and ChatGPT as generative image tools, but does not specify their generation-model versions; the screening references to other image tools describe participants' prior use, not the study engines (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3.4 and 4.1; p. 15, Appendix D.1; p. 16, Appendix D.5).
This is an original system/user-study paper, not a synthesis; synthesis counts and pooled-effect fields appropriately remain at their defaults (PDF pp. 6-9, Sections 4-4.3; pp. 14-17, Appendix D).
summary: The 15-person counterbalanced comparison of Creo and ChatGPT reports no random assignment, and its version, sample count, first-to-final distance statistics, and exclusion from core are supported. Four corrections complete outcome coding; the numerical results and the distinction between within-session anchoring and qualitative across-person diversity remain unchanged.
